svg.title: Where Secure by Design, ASVS, and AISVS touch the lifecycle
svg.desc: Secure by Design (OWASP checklist 0.5), Decided before code, in planning and design: Planning, main: Capture security requirements: its first step, named Planning.; Analysis, in part: Part of the same first step: the requirements the design must meet.; Design, main: Its core: architecture, the principles and patterns, the five-part review checklist, peer review, risk triage, and threat modeling (steps 2 to 8).; Implementation, in part: Handoff to development with the finished design (step 9).; Testing & Integration, in part: Plans the tests in design: ASVS-aligned and negative tests (MT-03, MT-04).; Maintenance, in part: Design-drift watch (step 10); logging, alerts, and a rehearsed incident plan chosen up front (MT-01, MT-02, MT-06). ASVS (OWASP 5.0), Requirements to build to, and to verify against: Planning, in part: Choose a level, 1 to 3, from what the app holds; the requirements double as a checklist.; Analysis, main: Which requirements apply; each chapter's documentation section says what to decide and write down (V2.1, V8.1, V15.1).; Design, in part: Architecture requirements (V1.1, V15.2) and recorded decisions, such as the inventory of cryptography (V11.1).; Implementation, main: Build to the 17 chapters: encoding, validation, sign-in, sessions, authorization, cryptography, and more.; Testing & Integration, main: Its purpose: verify each requirement. It is the Application Security Verification Standard.; Maintenance, in part: Deadlines for updating dependencies (V15.1, V15.2), configuration (V13), and security logging (V16). AISVS (OWASP 1.0), For apps that use AI, and, in its Appendix C, apps built with AI: Planning, in part: A workflow that covers every phase and keeps its security gates (AC.1); qualify the AI tools and model their threats (AC.2).; Analysis, in part: Write down the AI threat scenarios behind each guardrail (AC.1).; Design, main: Access control for AI parts (C5), agents and orchestration (C9), MCP (C10), memory and vector stores (C8).; Implementation, main: Training data (C1), input (C2), output (C7), the model supply chain (C6); prompts (AC.3) and checking AI-written code (AC.4).; Testing & Integration, main: Model validation (C3.2), adversarial robustness (C11), and adversarial testing (AC.6).; Maintenance, main: Controlled deployment and rollback (C3.3), monitoring and drift (C12), and containing a compromise (AC.14).
svg.text: Where Secure by Design, ASVS, and AISVS touch the lifecycle
Each framework against OWASP's six phases. “Main” marks a phase the framework is chiefly for; “In part”, one it reaches into for part of its work.
reaches into part of this phase

Sources: the frameworks as StackVet carries them (data/frameworks): the Secure by Design checklist's ten process steps and its controls, ASVS 5.0's chapters and sections, AISVS 1.0's chapters and Appendix C.
Phases: After the typical SDLC diagram on OWASP's Integration Standards page, owasp.github.io/www-project-integration-standards/writeups/owasp_in_sdlc.
